verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct (TN): after the agent finished, the held-out verifier compared `airport.duckdb` against `gold.duckdb` and reported that `fct_arrivals__malaysia_summary` did not match despite identical 7×5 shapes [1]. The task required completing the missing dbt core models so `dbt run` materializes Malaysian arrival summaries and an airport distance matrix in `airport.duckdb` [2], and the reference solution does so by adding core SQL that groups latest-day non-codeshare arrivals by `arrival_iata` joined to `base_airports.iata` without deduplicating raw rows [3]. The agent explored the project, fixed the staging Haversine formula, created both core models, ran `dbt run`, and initially hit the `unique` test on `base_arrivals__malaysia.full_url` [4]; it then added `select distinct *` deduplication in `base_arrivals__malaysia.sql` [5], which made all 12 packaged dbt tests pass [6] and led it to declare success [7], but that dedup removed three duplicate arrival rows and lowered flight counts (e.g., Kuching 55 and Marudi 4 in its own spot-check [8]) so the materialized summary no longer matched gold [1]. Reproducing the agent's final models in this sandbox reproduces the verifier failure on arrivals [9], and independently the agent's Haversine cosine fix also makes the distance matrix diverge from gold even when arrivals logic otherwise matches [10], whereas applying only the reference core models to the initial workspace passes both table comparisons [11]. The agent relied on schema-level dbt tests and informal distance spot-checks rather than validating aggregate flight counts against expected outputs, so it did not genuinely accomplish the task.

judge_verdict.summary: The agent built dbt fact models and ran dbt successfully, but incorrect deduplication in the base arrivals model produced wrong flight counts that failed gold comparison.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct. The held-out verifier compared the agent's post-run `/workspace/airport.duckdb` against gold and reported `binary_reward` 0 because `fct_arrivals__malaysia_summary` had matching shape (7×5) but mismatched values [1][2]. The task required completing the dbt project to aggregate Malaysian arrival flight counts and airport distances, then running `dbt run` [3]. The reference solution adds the two missing core fact models without altering `base_arrivals__malaysia`, counting latest-date non-code-share arrivals from the undeduplicated base and pivoting distances with `dbt_utils.pivot` [4][5]. The agent did create those core models and fix the staging haversine, but after `dbt test` flagged a `full_url` uniqueness failure in `base.yml` [6], it deduplicated `base_arrivals__malaysia` by `full_url` [7][8] even though the prompt never asked to change base-layer grain. That dedup lowered flight counts (e.g., Kuching 55 and Marudi 4 in the agent's own final validation [9]) below what the reference arrivals model produces when it counts directly from the undeduplicated base [3], which is why the verifier rejected the table even though row counts and dbt tests looked healthy. The agent declared success after `dbt test` passed [10], but its self-checks only inspected row counts and plausibility, not equality to the expected summary values, so it missed the counting error the verifier caught.

judge_verdict.summary: The agent built plausible dbt models and ran dbt successfully, but DISTINCT deduplication and a haversine rewrite produced output tables that do not match the gold standard.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a genuine agent-fault failure—the verifier's FAIL is correct. After the agent finished, the held-out verifier compared `airport.duckdb` against `gold.duckdb` and reported `binary_reward` 0 because `fct_arrivals__malaysia_summary` had the right 7×5 shape but wrong cell values [1][2]. The task asked the agent to complete/fix dbt models so `dbt run` materializes correct Malaysian arrival summaries and airport-distance tables in DuckDB [3]. The reference path only replaces the two core fact models, counting non-code-shared arrivals on the latest date from the unmodified `base_arrivals__malaysia` feed without any DISTINCT deduplication [4][5]. The agent did create those fact models and execute `dbt run`, but it also rewrote upstream models in ways that change the graded outputs: after `dbt test` surfaced three duplicate `full_url` rows [6], it added `select distinct` to `base_arrivals__malaysia.sql` at step 30 to satisfy the unique schema test [7], which removes arrival rows that the gold counts still include, and at step 8 it rewrote the staging haversine to insert `cos(a_lat)*cos(b_lat)` even though the reference leaves the original staging model untouched [5][8]. Its own validation was limited to `dbt test` not-null/unique checks and a single distance spot-check that already showed Bario→Bakalalan at 30.83 km [9]; it nonetheless closed claiming all transformations were correct [10]. Because the submitted database does not match gold on the primary fact table (and the rewritten haversine would also break the distance matrix), the agent did not truly solve the task and TN is the right classification.
